title: FairAIED: Navigating Fairness, Bias, and Ethics in Educational AI Applications

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review and analysis of case studies where AI models (e.g., in college admissions or early warning systems) systematically disadvantage applicants or students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds or under-resourced schools.

Survey of literature and case studies demonstrating disparate impacts on racial minorities, such as AI-based early warning systems over-identifying African American and Hispanic students as "at-risk" due to historically biased data.

Review of educational AI applications, such as AI-driven career guidance systems, that perpetuate traditional gender stereotypes by recommending distinct career paths (e.g., STEM vs. humanities) based on gender.

Examination of representation and measurement biases in automated essay scoring systems, which frequently penalize English as a Second Language (ESL) students and users of African American Vernacular English (AAVE) due to training on Standard American English.

Analysis of exclusion bias in educational tools that fail to provide necessary assistive features (e.g., closed captions, alternative text), thereby systematically disadvantaging students with visual, hearing, or cognitive impairments.
